from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites & Intuition", [
            "A kernel is a small, sliding window.",
            "Matrices store our input image data.",
            "Convolution performs element-wise multiplication and summation."
        ])

        # Animation Setup
        # Create input grid
        input_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7, color=WHITE) for _ in range(9)])
        input_grid.arrange_in_grid(3, 3, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(input_grid, "B2")
        input_label = Text("Input", font_size=20).next_to(input_grid, UP)
        
        # Create kernel
        kernel = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.23, color="#FF5733", fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(9)])
        kernel.arrange_in_grid(3, 3, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(kernel, "B2")
        kernel_label = Text("Kernel", font_size=20, color="#FF5733").next_to(kernel, DOWN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(Create(kernel), Write(kernel_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(input_grid), Write(input_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Simulating convolution action: moving kernel
        self.play(kernel.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.8))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(kernel), FadeOut(kernel_label))
        result = Text("Sum: 15", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(result, "E3")
        self.play(Write(result))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Future: Feature Maps in AI", [
            "Deep learning learns these kernel values automatically.",
            "AI uses these features to recognize objects.",
            "Computers now see the world like humans."
        ])
        self.lecture.set_opacity(0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color("#88CCFF")

        # Object classification result
        result_label = Text("Dog", font_size=36, color=GREEN).add_background_rectangle()
        self.place_at_grid(result_label, "F5")

outline.topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 min)
sections.content: Define a 'Kernel' (a small sliding window) and a 'Matrix' (input data). Explain that a convolution is an element-wise multiplication followed by a sum, representing the 'local influence' of pixels on their neighbors.
sections.example: Imagine a 3x3 grid of pixels representing a camera sensor. If one pixel is very bright, how does it share its light with the neighbors? Convolution is the mathematical 'sharing' mechanism.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Sliding & Computing (1.5 min)
sections.content: Visualize the kernel sliding over the input matrix. Show the step-by-step math: (Input_pixel * Kernel_weight) summed across the kernel area. Highlight how the output matrix size changes relative to stride.
sections.example: An animated 'Flashlight' (Kernel) scanning over a dark map (Input). As the flashlight hits an area, it calculates the 'intensity' of that spot, creating a new, highlighted map.

sections.title: Applications: Image Processing (1.5 min)
sections.content: Introduce specific kernels: A blur kernel (average of neighbors) vs. an edge-detection kernel (difference between neighbors). Emphasize how changing the kernel coefficients changes the perception of the image.
sections.example: A cat's photo. When passed through a 'Blur' kernel, the cat looks soft. When passed through an 'Edge Detection' (Sobel) kernel, the cat's whiskers and outlines glow bright white against a black background.

sections.title: The Future: Feature Maps in AI (1 min)
sections.content: Connect the manual kernels to Deep Learning. Explain that Neural Networks 'learn' the best kernel values automatically to identify objects, allowing robots to see the world like humans do.
sections.example: A robot learning to recognize a dog. The first layer detects ears, the second layer detects snouts, and the final layer triggers the label 'Dog'—all driven by millions of learned discrete convolutions.
